title: Panels
sub: StackPanel, WrapPanel, DockPanel: how each one lays out
cards/0/title: The panel decides who goes where
cards/0/body:
StackPanel: one after another, top to bottom or left to right.
WrapPanel: in a row, and whatever does not fit moves to the next line, like words in text.
DockPanel: docks children to the edges, and the last one fills the rest.
Grid: rows and columns. That is the next lesson.
cards/1/task: Build a classic window: header at the top, menu on the left, status at the bottom, content takes the rest.
cards/2/q: Why does the menu in a DockPanel reach all the way down, while the status bar only sits to its right?
cards/2/options/0: The menu is docked before the status bar: DockPanel hands out space in child order
cards/2/options/1: The designer drew it that way
cards/2/explain: Swap the children in the markup, and the status bar spans the whole bottom while the menu gets shorter.
cards/3/task: The window is narrow, 220 px. Make the items wrap to a new line when they do not fit.
cards/4/q: What does a horizontal StackPanel do when its children do not fit the width?
cards/4/options/0: Nothing: they run off the edge of the window
cards/4/options/1: Wraps them to a new line
cards/4/explain: Wrapping is WrapPanel's job. StackPanel gives children as much as they ask for in its direction.
cards/5/task: A toolbar: everything in one row, left to right, at full height.
cards/6/q: Dock the menu to the left edge
cards/6/explain: The content comes last, so it fills the rest.
cards/7/q: Match each panel to its behavior
cards/7/pairs/2/1: To the edges, last one fills the rest
cards/8/q: What is true? Select all that apply.
cards/8/options/0: Child order matters in a DockPanel
cards/8/options/1: The last child of a DockPanel fills the rest
cards/8/options/2: StackPanel wraps items to a new line
cards/8/options/3: WrapPanel wraps items to a new line
cards/8/explain: The last child fills the rest unless LastChildFill is turned off.
